mainTopic: Who a husband can give קינוי about: עריות, a קטן, a שחוף, a נכרי and an animal, and what the words שכבת זרע exclude.
overview: The גמרא first explains why the משנה needed to say that a husband can warn his wife even about an ערוה, a man she is already forbidden to. It then asks what the משנה's words 'one who is not a man' exclude. A שחוף cannot be meant, because שמואל rules that one can warn about him and that he disqualifies a woman from תרומה. A נכרי cannot be meant either, because רב המנונא rules the same about him, with support from רבי יוחנן. The גמרא explains why each of these rulings needed to be said. רב פפא concludes that the words exclude an animal, since there is no זנות with an animal, and this is proven from the פסוק of אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב. The גמרא then asks what the words שכבת זרע come to exclude. After answers from רב ששת, רבא and אביי are each challenged, it settles that they exclude a warning about contact through other limbs. The amud ends as שמואל begins a new teaching about whom a man should marry.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed to include forbidden relatives
steps.stepSummary: Without the משנה, we might have thought קינוי only works when the affair itself creates a new prohibition, not with an ערוה who is already forbidden. The משנה teaches that it works even then.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought: the Torah says 'she was defiled' twice, once to forbid her to her husband and once to forbid her to the man she sinned with. That only applies where this sin is what makes her forbidden to him. But here, since she is already forbidden to him as a relative, maybe קינוי does not apply. So the משנה teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question from just before this: why did the משנה need to say that a husband can warn about forbidden relatives? It explains the mistake we might have made.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The double word נטמאה teaches that a סוטה becomes forbidden both to her husband and to the בועל. That might suggest the whole process is about creating a new prohibition with the בועל. With an ערוה she is already forbidden to him, so we might think קינוי does not apply, and the משנה rules out that idea.

steps.terutzMaskana: קינוי applies even regarding an ערוה.

steps.title: No warning about a minor: the source
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's exclusion of a קטן and gives the source: the Torah says 'a man'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: except for a minor, etc. The Torah says 'a man', and not a minor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, which excludes a קטן, and gives the פסוק behind it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרשה of סוטה speaks of 'a man' lying with her. A קטן is not called a man, so a husband cannot do קינוי about a קטן.

steps.title: What does 'one who is not a man' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: The משנה also excludes 'one who is not a man'. The גמרא asks who that is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And 'one who is not a man': what does that come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'one who is not a man'. This sets up the next move, where it tries out an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן was already excluded, so this phrase must refer to someone else. The גמרא wants to know who.

keyTerms.meaning: One who is not a man

steps.title: It can't mean a שחוף, because of שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests 'not a man' means a שחוף, but objects from שמואל, who says one can warn about a שחוף and that he disqualifies a woman from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it excludes a שחוף, but שמואל said: one can warn about a שחוף, and he disqualifies a woman from eating תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the answer that 'not a man' means a שחוף, then immediately attacks it with a ruling of שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שחוף is a sick man who cannot complete relations normally, so he seemed like a good fit for 'not a man'. But שמואל treats him as a full man for קינוי, so the משנה cannot be excluding him.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a proposed answer)
A sick, weakened man who cannot complete relations normally
But didn't he say! (introduces a challenge)

phrases.english: If you say it excludes a שחוף,
but didn't שמואל say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a possible answer to the question and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'one who is not a man' means a שחוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל says קינוי works for a שחוף, so the משנה cannot be excluding him.

steps.title: Isn't שמואל's first ruling obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses on שמואל's ruling and asks why he needed to say that one can warn about a שחוף.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'One can warn about him': that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא steps aside to look at שמואל's first ruling and asks why it needed to be said at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A שחוף is still a man, so it seems clear that קינוי applies to him. The גמרא wants to know what new idea שמואל was teaching.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious!

phrases.english: 'One can warn about him': that is obvious!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that קינוי applies to a שחוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שחוף is a man, so the ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Why שמואל had to say it: 'lying of seed'
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought a שחוף is excluded because the פסוק speaks of שכבת זרע, which he cannot do. שמואל teaches that קינוי still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the Torah says 'and a man lay with her a lying of seed', and this man is not able to do that. So שמואל teaches us that one can still warn about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake שמואל was blocking: that the words 'lying of seed' leave out a שחוף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes relations with seed, and a שחוף cannot release seed normally. We might have read that as a condition for סוטה. שמואל teaches that the act counts even without that.

steps.title: Isn't שמואל's second ruling obvious too?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about שמואל's second ruling, that a שחוף disqualifies a woman from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he disqualifies her from תרומה': that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why שמואל needed to say that a שחוף disqualifies a woman from eating תרומה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Forbidden relations disqualify a בת כהן from תרומה, and a שחוף is a man. So the ruling seems clear, and the גמרא asks what it adds.

A כהן's daughter, who may eat תרומה

phrases.english: 'And he disqualifies her from תרומה': that is obvious!

steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that a שחוף disqualifies a woman from תרומה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He is a man, so the ruling seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Why שמואל had to say it: 'his seed'
steps.stepSummary: We might have thought only a man who can have children disqualifies a woman from תרומה, based on the פסוק 'he shall not profane his seed'. שמואל teaches that a שחוף disqualifies too.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the Torah says 'he shall not profane his seed'. One who has seed disqualifies, one who has no seed does not. So שמואל teaches us that even a שחוף disqualifies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the mistake שמואל was blocking: that disqualifying from תרומה depends on being able to have children.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about a כהן speaks of 'his seed', which could suggest only a man able to have children can make a woman unfit. שמואל teaches that this is not a condition. Both of his rulings stand, so 'one who is not a man' in the משנה cannot mean a שחוף. The next step tries another reading.

keyTerms.meaning: Profane, make unfit
His seed (offspring)
One who has
One who does not have

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל treats a שחוף as a full man: one can warn about him, and he disqualifies a woman from תרומה. So the משנה's 'one who is not a man' must mean someone else. Step 16 gives the final answer: an animal.

phrases.english: You might have said:

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains the mistaken reading of the פסוק that שמואל rules out.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a man able to have children disqualifies a woman from תרומה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A שחוף also disqualifies a woman from תרומה.

steps.title: Maybe 'not a man' excludes a gentile, but רב המנונא says otherwise
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that 'not a man' in the משנה excludes a נכרי. It then challenges this from רב המנונא, who says קינוי works for a נכרי and that he disqualifies a woman from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, maybe the משנה comes to exclude a gentile? But didn't רב המנונא say: a gentile, one can warn about him, and he disqualifies a woman from תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The שחוף reading did not work, so the גמרא tries a new reading: 'not a man' means a נכרי. Right away it attacks this reading with a statement of רב המנונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה excluded a נכרי, then a husband could not warn his wife about one. רב המנונא says the opposite: קינוי does work for a נכרי, and a נכרי also disqualifies a woman from תרומה. So the new reading clashes with an אמורא's ruling, just as the שחוף reading clashed with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (the first idea failed, so try another)
to exclude
a gentile
one can give a warning (קינוי) about him

phrases.english: Rather, does it come to exclude a gentile?
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה's phrase 'not a man.' The שחוף reading failed, so now we try a gentile.

phrases.english: But didn't Rav Hamnuna say:
A gentile: one can give a warning about him

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שחוף reading was rejected and שמואל's rulings were explained, the גמרא offers a new reading of 'not a man' and challenges it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that 'not a man' in the משנה excludes a נכרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב המנונא rules that קינוי works for a נכרי, so the משנה cannot be excluding him.

steps.title: Why say a gentile can be warned about? Isn't it obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pauses on רב המנונא's first ruling and asks why it needed to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one can warn about a gentile: that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to look closely at רב המנונא's first ruling. It asks: why tell us something so obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: An act with a נכרי is still a forbidden act, so we would expect קינוי to apply. A ruling that seems obvious makes us ask what wrong idea it is coming to block. The answer comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: it is obvious (so why say it?)

phrases.english: One can give a warning about him: that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Zooms in on the first half of רב המנונא's statement quoted in step 9, the same way steps 5–8 looked at שמואל.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's ruling that קינוי works for a נכרי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems self-evident, so it seems there was no need to say it.

steps.title: We might have thought סוטה only applies when the act itself creates a new prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The word נטמאה appears twice: once making her forbidden to her husband, once to the man she was with. We might have thought סוטה applies only when this act makes her newly forbidden to him. Since she was already forbidden to a נכרי, רב המנונא had to teach that קינוי still applies.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: 'she was defiled,' 'she was defiled' appears twice, once for the husband and once for the paramour. That applies where she becomes forbidden through this act. But here, since she is already forbidden to him, say it does not apply. So he teaches us that it does.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 10. It shows a wrong idea that רב המנונא's ruling comes to block.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two mentions of נטמאה teach that a סוטה becomes forbidden both to her husband and to the בועל. We might think the whole סוטה process is only for a case where this act creates that prohibition to the בועל. A Jewish woman was always forbidden to a נכרי, so the act changes nothing there. רב המנונא teaches that קינוי still works.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the two mentions of נטמאה tie סוטה to her becoming forbidden to the בועל, a woman already forbidden to a נכרי would not be included.
steps.terutzMaskana: קינוי works even for a נכרי, even though she was already forbidden to him.

steps.title: Why say a gentile disqualifies from תרומה? Isn't it obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the same question about רב המנונא's second ruling, that a נכרי disqualifies a woman from תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that he disqualifies her from תרומה: that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks why רב המנונא's second ruling was needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If even a forbidden Jewish man disqualifies a בת כהן from תרומה, a נכרי surely should too. So the גמרא asks what wrong idea this ruling comes to block.

keyTerms.meaning: disqualifies
the holy portion that only כהנים and their households may eat

phrases.english: And he disqualifies her from teruma: that is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 10, now on the second half of רב המנונא's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב המנונא's ruling that a נכרי disqualifies a woman from תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling seems self-evident, so it seems there was no need to say it.

steps.title: We might have thought only someone who can marry her disqualifies her
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'when she shall be to a strange man,' and 'be to' means marriage. So we might think only a man who could marry her disqualifies her, and a נכרי cannot. רב המנונא teaches that a נכרי does disqualify, based on רבי יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: the Torah says 'And a כהן's daughter, if she shall be to a strange man.' One who can marry her, yes; one who cannot marry her, no. So he teaches us that a gentile disqualifies her, as we learn from רבי יוחנן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 12 with a wrong idea that comes from the wording of a פסוק. Then it points to רבי יוחנן as the source, which it quotes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word תהיה ('shall be to') is marriage language. So we might think only a man whose קידושין would work can disqualify her from תרומה. קידושין with a נכרי does not work, so he would not count. רב המנונא teaches that he still disqualifies her, and the proof is from רבי יוחנן.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because 'shall be to' means marriage, only a man who can validly marry her would disqualify her, and a נכרי cannot.
steps.terutzMaskana: A נכרי does disqualify her from תרומה, as רבי יוחנן's teaching shows.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's source: a gentile or slave disqualifies a woman
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי ישמעאל learns from the פסוק 'a כהן's daughter who becomes a widow or divorcée.' She goes back to eating תרומה only after a man with whom widowhood and divorce are possible. A נכרי or עבד does not fit that, so after being with one she does not go back to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי ישמעאל: How do we know that a gentile or a slave who was with a כהן's daughter, a לוי's daughter, or a ישראל's daughter disqualified her? Because it says 'And a כהן's daughter, if she becomes a widow or divorcée.' That means one with whom she can be widowed or divorced. This leaves out a gentile and a slave, with whom she cannot be widowed or divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the teaching of רבי יוחנן that it just mentioned. It is the proof that a נכרי disqualifies a woman.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lets a בת כהן go back to eating תרומה after being widowed or divorced. Widowhood and divorce only exist where there was a real marriage. So the permission to go back only covers a man whose marriage to her would work. A נכרי or עבד has no valid marriage with her, so he is not covered, and she stays disqualified. This removes the wrong idea from step 13.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know?

steps.title: So what does 'one who is not a man' exclude?
steps.stepSummary: Since a נכרי is included, the גמרא asks what the exclusion 'one who is not a man' comes to leave out.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, what does it come to exclude?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has just shown that a נכרי is included in קינוי, so it asks what the words 'one who is not a man' now leave out. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier it seemed that 'one who is not a man' might mean a נכרי. רב המנונא's rulings showed that a נכרי does count, so that reading falls away. Now the exclusion needs a new target.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather / but then (introduces a new attempt after an idea fell away)
to exclude
what

phrases.english: But rather, to exclude what?
phrases.notes: This refers to the words in the משנה, 'and one who is not a man.' What are they leaving out, now that a נכרי counts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from the conclusion that a נכרי is included, which left the exclusion without a target.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What case the phrase 'one who is not a man' excludes.

steps.title: It excludes an animal
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the phrase excludes an animal, because there is no זנות with an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It excludes an animal, because there is no זנות with an animal.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that 'one who is not a man' leaves out an animal. If a husband warns his wife about an animal, it is not a קינוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of סוטה are about זנות, forbidden relations of a married woman. רב פפא holds that relations with an animal do not count as זנות in this sense. So קינוי does not apply to it.

keyTerms.meaning: an animal
harlotry; forbidden relations that make a woman a זונה

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
To exclude an animal,
since there is no harlotry with an animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase excludes an animal, since there is no זנות with an animal.

steps.title: Where do we learn there is no זנות with an animal?
steps.stepSummary: רבא מפרזקיא asks רב אשי for the source of the rule that there is no זנות with an animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא מפרזקיא said to רב אשי: From where do we know what the רבנן said, that there is no זנות with an animal?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא מפרזקיא asks for the source of רב פפא's reason. This question sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב פפא's answer stands on the rule that there is no זנות with an animal. רבא מפרזקיא is not arguing with it. He wants to know which פסוק it comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where is this matter? (asking for a source)
the Sages

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא מִפַּרְזִקְיָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי:
phrases.english: Rava of Parzakya said to Rav Ashi:
From where is this matter
that the Sages said: there is no harlotry with an animal?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the reason given in step 16.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for the rule that there is no זנות with an animal.

steps.title: The פסוק about אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי brings the פסוק that forbids bringing a זונה's payment or the price of a dog as a קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'You shall not bring the payment of a זונה or the price of a dog' into the house of ה'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי starts his answer by quoting the פסוק that forbids two things as קרבנות: אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב. The next step uses a ברייתא to show how this proves the point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On its own, the פסוק just lists two forbidden things. The proof only works once we see, in the next step, that the reverse cases are allowed. So this step sets up the base text.

keyTerms.meaning: the payment given to a זונה
the price paid for a dog
as it is written

phrases.english: As it is written:
"You shall not bring the hire of a harlot
or the price of a dog, etc."
phrases.notes: The 'etc.' points to the rest of the פסוק, which ends 'for both of them are an abomination.' The next step uses those words.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: לֹא תָבִיא אֶתְנַן זוֹנָה וּמְחִיר כֶּלֶב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to רבא מפרזקיא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the פסוק of אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב, explained in the next step.

steps.title: 'Two and not four': a dog's payment is permitted
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a dog's payment and a זונה's price are permitted, since 'both of them' means two and not four. This shows that a payment for relations with an animal is not זנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was taught: The payment of a dog and the price of a זונה are permitted, as it says 'both of them': two, and not four.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא says the reverse cases are allowed as קרבנות: payment for relations with a dog, and money paid to buy a זונה. This finishes the proof that there is no זנות with an animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'both of them' limit the ban to the two cases in the פסוק, not four. So a payment given for relations with a dog is not treated like אתנן זונה. That shows the תורה does not treat relations with an animal as זנות.

keyTerms.meaning: permitted
'both of them' (words from the פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: There is no זנות with an animal. We learn this from 'both of them': the payment for relations with a dog is not forbidden like a זונה's payment. So 'one who is not a man' excludes an animal from קינוי.
steps.confusionAlert: The two allowed cases are the reverse of the פסוק. 'אתנן כלב' is payment for relations with a dog, and 'מחיר זונה' is money paid to buy her. Don't mix them up with אתנן זונה and מחיר כלב.
steps.whyThisMatters: This proof backs up רב פפא's answer from step 16, so the exclusion 'one who is not a man' is settled as an animal.

phrases.english: And it is taught:
the hire of a dog and the price of a harlot are permitted,
phrases.notes: These are the reverse of the פסוק. 'Hire of a dog' means payment given for relations with a dog.

phrases.english: as it is stated: "both of them,"
two and not four.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתַנְיָא: אֶתְנַן כֶּלֶב וּמְחִיר זוֹנָה מוּתָּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun with the פסוק in step 18.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that there is no זנות with an animal.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'גם שניהם' as 'two and not four,' which permits the payment for relations with a dog.

steps.title: Then why does the פסוק say שכבת זרע?
steps.stepSummary: Since a warning applies even where there is no release of seed, the גמרא asks why the פסוק needs the words שכבת זרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, why do I need the words 'שכבת זרע'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the פסוק in the סוטה section says 'שכבת זרע' if the law does not depend on seed. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, שמואל ruled that a husband can warn about a שחוף, a man who cannot release seed. If seed is not required, the words 'שכבת זרע' seem to teach nothing. The גמרא wants to know their job.

keyTerms.meaning: lying with seed (the פסוק's phrase for relations)
why do I need it?

phrases.english: But rather, "carnally [shikhvat zera]", why do I need it?
phrases.notes: במדבר 5:13. This goes back to שמואל's ruling about a שחוף, where there is no seed at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the animal topic and returns to שמואל's ruling about a שחוף.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's ruling that קינוי applies to a שחוף.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If seed is not needed, the פסוק's words 'שכבת זרע' would seem to have no purpose.

steps.title: שכבת זרע comes to exclude 'something else'
steps.stepSummary: The words שכבת זרע are needed for a ברייתא's teaching that they exclude 'something else.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed for what was taught: 'שכבת זרע' excludes something else.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the words 'שכבת זרע' have a different job. As a ברייתא teaches, they exclude 'something else,' so they do not show that a שחוף is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words are not there to require seed. They limit which kind of act a warning can be about. So שמואל's ruling about a שחוף stays in place.

keyTerms.meaning: it is needed for (a different teaching)
excluding something else

steps.whatToRemember: 'שכבת זרע' does not mean seed is required. It excludes 'something else,' so a warning about a שחוף still works.

phrases.english: It is needed for that which is taught:
"Shikhvat zera" excludes something else.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reassigning the words of the פסוק to a different teaching
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'שכבת זרע' would mean seed is required, so a שחוף would be left out.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'שכבת זרע' excludes 'something else,' so שמואל's ruling about a שחוף stands.

steps.title: What is the 'something else'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the ברייתא meant when it said שכבת זרע leaves out 'something else.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'something else'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question about the ברייתא from the last step. It is setting up a set of answers that will follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the words שכבת זרע leave out a 'דבר אחר' but did not say what that is. The rest of this section tries to name that case.

keyTerms.meaning: Something else. Here it means a different kind of act that the פסוק leaves out.
Lying with release of seed. These are the words in the סוטה פסוק.

phrases.english: What is "something else"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks what the vague phrase in the ברייתא from step 21 means.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case does 'דבר אחר' refer to?

steps.title: רב ששת: a warning about relations שלא כדרכה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת says the פסוק leaves out a case where the husband warned his wife about relations שלא כדרכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: It leaves out a case where he warned her about relations in an unusual way.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת gives the first answer. He says the excluded case is a קינוי about relations שלא כדרכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ששת's idea is that שכבת זרע describes normal relations. So a warning about relations in an unusual way would not make her a סוטה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaving out; except for.
He warned her. This is the husband's warning (קינוי) not to be alone with a certain man.
Not in the usual way, meaning unusual relations.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
It leaves out where he warned her about relations not in the usual way.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: פְּרָט לְשֶׁקִּינֵּא לָהּ שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'something else' is a קינוי about relations שלא כדרכה.

steps.title: רבא: the Torah counts both ways as relations
steps.stepSummary: רבא challenges רב ששת: the פסוק משכבי אשה shows that unusual relations also count as relations.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to him: Unusual relations? It is written 'the lyings of a woman'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבא attacks רב ששת's answer. He says the Torah treats unusual relations as real relations, so they cannot be what is left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word משכבי is plural, meaning 'lyings', so it teaches that there are two ways of relations with a woman. Both count the same. So a warning about relations שלא כדרכה is a real warning.

keyTerms.meaning: The lyings of a woman. The plural form teaches two ways of relations.
It is written.

phrases.english: Rava said to him:
Not in the usual way? "The lyings of a woman" is written!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 18:22. 'Lyings' is plural, so it covers both ways.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא: שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ, ״מִשְׁכְּבֵי אִשָּׁה״ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ששת's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ששת's claim that relations שלא כדרכה are left out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק already shows that unusual relations are full relations, so they cannot be excluded.

steps.title: רבא: a warning about contact through other limbs
steps.stepSummary: רבא suggests instead that the excluded case is a warning about contact through other limbs.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: It leaves out where he warned her about contact through other limbs.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב ששת's answer fell, רבא offers a new answer. The excluded case is a קינוי about contact through other limbs, which is not relations at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows that the earlier answer is dropped. רבא picks a case that is clearly not relations, so שכבת זרע would leave it out.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It drops the earlier answer and gives a new one.
By way of limbs, meaning contact through other body parts, not relations.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
It leaves out where he warned her about contact through other limbs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: פְּרָט לְשֶׁקִּינֵּא לָהּ דֶּרֶךְ אֵבָרִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב ששת's answer after the challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New identification of the excluded case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The excluded case is relations שלא כדרכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The excluded case is a קינוי about contact through other limbs.

steps.title: אביי: that is only פריצותא, so why would we need a פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: אביי objects that contact through limbs is only immodest behavior, which never makes a woman forbidden, so the פסוק has no need to leave it out.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: That is just immodest behavior. Does the Torah forbid a woman because of immodest behavior?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבא's answer. Contact through other limbs is plainly not something that forbids her, so it seems no פסוק is needed to teach that.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק should not come to teach something that is already obvious. Since פריצותא alone never forbids a woman to her husband, a warning about it would clearly not count anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Immodest behavior, not actual relations.
Merely, just.
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
That is just immodest behavior,
and did the Merciful One forbid her because of immodest behavior?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: פְּרִיצוּתָא בְּעָלְמָא הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבא's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that the פסוק leaves out a warning about contact through limbs.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That case is obvious, because פריצותא never forbids a woman, so the extra words would be wasted.

steps.title: אביי: a warning about נשיקה (contact without entry)
steps.stepSummary: אביי suggests the excluded case is a warning about נשיקה, meaning genital contact without real entry.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: It leaves out where he warned her about נשיקה.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a third answer. The פסוק leaves out a קינוי about נשיקה, which is genital contact without entry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is closer to relations than contact through limbs, so it is not obvious and the פסוק would need to teach it. The words שכבת זרע show that only real relations count.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means genital contact without entry, not a kiss.

steps.confusionAlert: In this סוגיא, נשיקה does NOT mean a kiss. It means genital contact without any entry.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
It leaves out where he warned her about contact without entry.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: פְּרָט לְשֶׁקִּינֵּא לָהּ בִּנְשִׁיקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רבא's answer after אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New identification of the excluded case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The excluded case is contact through other limbs.
steps.terutzMaskana: The excluded case is a קינוי about נשיקה.

steps.title: אביי's answer only works by one view of הערא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that אביי's answer works for the view that הערא is entry of the corona, but not for the view that הערא is נשיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says הערא is entry of the corona, and נשיקה is nothing, so the פסוק comes to leave out נשיקה. But for the one who says הערא is נשיקה, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges אביי's answer. By one opinion it works, but by the other opinion נשיקה is already the start of relations, so it cannot be left out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an argument about what counts as הערא, the first stage of relations. If it starts only with entry, then נשיקה is nothing and the פסוק can leave it out. If נשיקה itself is הערא, it counts as relations and אביי's answer fails.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well, but only for one view.
The first stage of relations.
Entry of the corona, a partial entry.
What is there to say? A sign of a real difficulty.

phrases.english: This works for the one who says
the first stage of relations is entry of the corona,
but contact without entry is nothing at all,
that is why the verse comes to leave out contact without entry.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הַעֲרָאָה זוֹ נְשִׁיקָה,
phrases.english: But for the one who says the first stage of relations is contact without entry,
what is there to say?
phrases.notes: By this view, contact without entry already counts as relations, so it can't be the case the פסוק leaves out.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר הַעֲרָאָה זוֹ הַכְנָסַת עֲטָרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges אביי's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's claim that the excluded case is נשיקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the view that נשיקה is הערא, נשיקה counts as relations, so the פסוק could not leave it out.

steps.title: Back to רבא: contact through limbs, because we might follow the בעל's objection
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to רבא's answer and explains why a פסוק was needed: we might have thought the law follows what the בעל objects to.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, it leaves out a warning about contact through other limbs. You might have said the Torah made this depend on the husband's objection, and the husband does object. So the פסוק teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to רבא's answer and answers אביי's challenge. The פסוק was needed because without it we might have thought a warning about contact through limbs counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said that case was obvious. The גמרא answers that it is not obvious, since the whole קינוי depends on what the בעל objects to, and a husband does mind this kind of contact. So the פסוק teaches that only a warning about real relations counts.

keyTerms.meaning: Really; actually. It returns to an earlier answer.
You might have said. It shows what we would wrongly think without the פסוק.
The husband's objection.
It teaches us otherwise.

steps.whatToRemember: The words שכבת זרע teach that a קינוי counts only if it is about real relations. A warning about contact through other limbs does not count, even though the בעל objects to it.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that קינוי is defined by the act of relations itself, and not just by whatever the husband does not want.

phrases.english: Really, it leaves out where he warned her about contact through other limbs.
And you might have said
that the Merciful One made it depend on the husband's objection,
and the husband does object to this,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the problem with אביי's answer, returns to רבא's answer and answers אביי's challenge from step 26.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing that a case thought obvious really needed a פסוק (מהו דתימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since קינוי depends on the בעל's objection, a warning about contact through limbs would count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק teaches that only a warning about real relations counts.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: דבר אחר is a קינוי about contact through other limbs; it does not make her a סוטה.

steps.title: שמואל begins a new teaching about whom a man should marry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves on from the discussion of the פסוק and starts a new statement by שמואל about marriage choices.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל says: It is better that a man marry...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic with a teaching from שמואל. This line only sets up his statement, and the full teaching continues right after it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier back-and-forth between אביי and רבא about what the פסוק leaves out is finished. Now שמואל begins a practical guideline that compares two kinds of marriage and tells us which is better. We only see the opening words here, so wait for the next lines to learn which choices he is comparing.

keyTerms.meaning: Should marry. It comes from the word נְשִׂיאָה, marriage, and here it has the sense of 'it is better that he marry'.
A person, here meaning a man looking for a wife.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read יִשָּׂא as a commandment that a man must marry this woman. It is the start of a comparison, meaning that one choice is better than another.

phrases.english: Shmuel says:
It is better that a man marry

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks away from the analysis of the פסוק in steps 25–29 and starts a new teaching.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל begins a guideline about which marriage is better. The full ruling continues in the next section.
